content: This study aimed to investigate whether the risk of mortality associated with sedentary behavior could be mitigated by engaging in moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (MVPA) when analyzed in a time-use framework. The research utilized data harmonized for MVPA from studies and meta-analyses identified through a PubMed search up to May 2018. Among 17 data custodians identified, seven provided data on sitting time, TV viewing time, or both. A dose-response meta-analysis was conducted to model the logarithmic relative risks of all-cause mortality against uncompensated sedentary behavior metabolic equivalent hours (USMh) using robust error meta-regression methods. The study included five harmonized cohorts for sitting time (258,688 participants) and four cohorts for TV viewing time (156,593 participants). The results demonstrated a significant association between sedentary behavior and mortality risk, which was attenuated with increased energy expenditure through MVPA modeled in a time-use manner. The thresholds for risk were identified as 7 USMh for sitting and 3 USMh for TV viewing. The findings suggest that exceeding a daily sedentary energy expenditure of 7 MET-hours for sitting or 3 MET-hours for TV viewing, beyond what is compensated by MVPA, is independently associated with all-cause mortality. These results emphasize the importance of considering concurrent MVPA when evaluating the health consequences of sedentary behavior. The USMh metric is proposed as a practical measure for assessing sedentary behavior. The study utilized harmonized data from cohort studies included in the 2016 Lancet meta-analysis by Ekelund et al. The outcomes addressed included total mortality, with the findings supporting the notion that sedentary behavior's impact on health is significantly influenced by the level of concurrent MVPA. This underscores the need for public health guidelines to incorporate strategies that balance sedentary time with adequate physical activity to mitigate adverse health outcomes.
